connectorUiConfig.descriptionMarkdown: The Prancer Data Connector provides the capability to ingest [Prancer CSPM](https://docs.prancer.io/web/CSPM/) and [PAC](https://docs.prancer.io/web/PAC/introduction/) findings into Microsoft Sentinel. Prancer's backend pushes findings directly to your workspace using the Azure Monitor Logs Ingestion API and a Data Collection Rule (DCR) that is auto-provisioned by the in-product connectivity wizard. Refer to the [Prancer Documentation](https://docs.prancer.io/web) for more information.

customs.name: Monitoring Metrics Publisher role
customs.description: Prancer's ingestion identity (the Microsoft Entra ID application registration created for your tenant during onboarding) must be assigned the **Monitoring Metrics Publisher** role, scoped to the Data Collection Rule used for ingestion. The in-product connectivity wizard assigns this role automatically when you complete setup; no manual role assignment is required unless your tenant enforces custom RBAC approval workflows.

instructionSteps.description: >**NOTE:** This connector uses the Azure Monitor [Logs Ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview) to push data directly from Prancer's backend into your workspace. This might result in additional data ingestion costs. Check the [Azure Monitor Logs pricing page](https://azure.microsoft.com/pricing/details/monitor/) for details.
STEP 1: Follow the documentation on the [Prancer Documentation Site](https://docs.prancer.io/web/) in order to set up a scan with an Azure cloud connector.
STEP 2: Once the scan is created go to the 'Third Party Integrations' menu for the scan and select Sentinel.

STEP 3: Follow the configuration wizard to select the target Log Analytics workspace and table (`PrancerFindings_CL`). The wizard automatically provisions the Data Collection Rule (DCR) and Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) required for ingestion, and grants Prancer's ingestion identity the Monitoring Metrics Publisher role on the new DCR — there is nothing to configure manually in Azure.

STEP 4: Once the wizard completes, Prancer's backend begins pushing scan findings directly to your workspace via the Logs Ingestion API. Data should start to appear in the `PrancerFindings_CL` table in Microsoft Sentinel for processing.

STEP 5 (optional): Deploy the **Prancer Connectivity Health Check** Azure Function (`Data Connectors/PrancerConnectivityHealthCheck/`) for an independent signal if ingestion ever stops — it periodically checks that `PrancerFindings_CL` is still receiving data and reports status via a webhook (and optionally a separate `PrancerConnectivityHealth_CL` table) that does not depend on the same Data Collection Rule it is monitoring. See that folder's readme for deployment steps. Not required for the connector to function — purely an added observability layer.

properties.query:
let SeverityRankFn = (sev: string) {
    case(
        sev == 'Critical', 1,
        sev == 'High', 2,
        sev == 'Medium', 3,
        sev == 'Low', 4,
        sev == 'Info' or sev == 'Informational', 5,
        99
    )
};
let Enriched = PrancerFindings_CL
| extend
    ResourceID = tostring(coalesce(Payload.message.resourceID, Payload.data.resourceID)),
    ApplicationName = tostring(coalesce(Payload.message.applicationName, Payload.data.applicationName)),
    RequestHeader = tostring(Payload.message.requestHeader),
    RequestBody = tostring(Payload.message.requestBody),
    ResponseHeader = tostring(Payload.message.responseHeader),
    ResponseBody = tostring(Payload.message.responseBody),
    AlertEvidence = tostring(Payload.alert.evidence),
    AlertSolution = tostring(coalesce(Payload.alert.solution, Solution)),
    CVSSScore = todouble(Payload.alert.cvss.cvss_score),
    CVSSVector = tostring(Payload.alert.cvss.vector_string),
    Snapshots = Payload.data.snapshots,
    RemediationDescription = tostring(Payload.data.remediation_description)
| extend SeverityRank = SeverityRankFn(Severity)
| extend DataQualityNotes = strcat(
      iff(isempty(FindingId), 'missing FindingId; ', ''),
      iff(isempty(Severity), 'missing Severity; ', ''),
      iff(isempty(CustomerId), 'missing CustomerId; ', ''),
      iff(isempty(DeviceProduct), 'missing DeviceProduct; ', ''),
      iff(isempty(ResourceID) and isempty(ApplicationName), 'missing ResourceID and ApplicationName; ', '')
  )
| extend IsDataQualityIssue = isnotempty(DataQualityNotes);
// Only de-duplicate rows that have a stable FindingId to key on ("latest wins" across
// re-ingested/updated records). Rows missing FindingId have no safe dedup key - collapsing
// them via arg_max(..., '') by an empty FindingId would merge every missing-FindingId finding
// into a single row, hiding exactly the data-quality problem DataQualityNotes/
// IsDataQualityIssue exist to surface. So those rows pass through unmodified instead.
union
    (Enriched | where isnotempty(FindingId) | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by FindingId),
    (Enriched | where isempty(FindingId))
| order by TimeGenerated desc

properties.description:
Weaker companion to the direct CSPM/SwarmHack exploited-resource correlation: flags SwarmHack findings
whose free-text KillChain path merely traverses a CSPM-flagged resource as a pivot point along the way
(lateral-movement corroboration), rather than the misconfigured resource being the final compromised
target. Matches CSPM Snapshots.path tokens against the KillChain text. VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08-11):
live production KillChain values observed so far are a flat scan-level execution-mode string (e.g. "full"),
not the per-finding multi-stage path text this rule is designed to text-match against. The query is
syntax-valid and executes safely with zero false positives against current data (confirmed live), but will
stay dormant until SwarmHack populates a genuinely descriptive per-finding KillChain value - track this
against real data before relying on this rule.
properties.displayName: SwarmHack kill chain traverses a CSPM-flagged resource
properties.query:
// CSPM posture data uses a long lookback (standing backlog); SwarmHack kill chains use a short one
// (near-real-time confirmation). has_any pre-filters cheaply on the full misconfig token list before
// the per-token mv-expand+contains+join, so the expensive per-token matching only runs on rows that
// already contain at least one candidate token somewhere in KillChain.
let MisconfigLookback = 30d;
let SwarmHackLookback = 1h;
let MisconfigResources = PrancerFindings
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(MisconfigLookback)
    | where DeviceProduct == 'cspm'
    | where isnotempty(Snapshots)
    | mv-expand Snapshots
    | extend MisconfigResourceKey = tostring(Snapshots.path), MisconfigResourceType = tostring(Snapshots.type)
    | where isnotempty(MisconfigResourceKey)
    | summarize CspmFindingIds = make_set(FindingId, 20) by CustomerId, MisconfigResourceKey, MisconfigResourceType;
let MisconfigTokenList = toscalar(MisconfigResources | summarize make_set(MisconfigResourceKey, 10000));
PrancerFindings
| where TimeGenerated > ago(SwarmHackLookback)
| where DeviceProduct == 'swarmhack'
| where isnotempty(KillChain)
| where KillChain has_any (MisconfigTokenList)
| mv-expand PotentialToken = MisconfigTokenList to typeof(string)
| where KillChain contains PotentialToken
| join kind=inner (MisconfigResources) on CustomerId, $left.PotentialToken == $right.MisconfigResourceKey
| summarize
    TraversedMisconfigResources = make_set(MisconfigResourceKey, 20),
    TraversedResourceTypes = make_set(MisconfigResourceType, 20),
    CorroboratingCspmFindingIds = make_set(CspmFindingIds, 20)
  by FindingId, ConfigId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Title, Severity, RiskScore, Confidence, KillChain, ResourceID, TimeGenerated
| extend PivotSummary = strcat('KillChain traverses ', array_length(TraversedMisconfigResources), ' CSPM-flagged resource(s) as pivot point(s)')

properties.description:
Force-escalates SwarmHack findings where CrownJewels contains a high-confidence sensitive target/asset
identification (confidence >= 0.8 on at least one CrownJewels entry) to Critical, overriding the nominal
Severity - correcting for the case where Severity scores the entry vulnerability rather than the value of
what SwarmHack actually identified as reachable. Only fires when the nominal Severity is not already
Critical. NOTE: validated against real production CrownJewels data (2026-08-11) - the real per-entry shape
is {category, value, confidence, context} (e.g. category="asrep_roast_target_list"), NOT the {name, type}
asset-taxonomy shape ({domain_controller, key_vault, ...}) originally assumed in the design ADR. This rule
was corrected to use the real shape; the category value space is not yet fully characterized against
production data (only one category observed so far), so the escalation trigger uses the per-entry
`confidence` field rather than a category allowlist that would need a larger, verified category taxonomy.
properties.displayName: Crown-jewel blast radius forces severity escalation
properties.query:
// Escalation threshold uses the per-entry `confidence` field on real CrownJewelSIEM objects
// ({category, value, confidence, context} - confirmed against real production data 2026-08-11).
// A fixed asset-type-taxonomy allowlist ({domain_controller, key_vault, ...}) is NOT used here since
// real `category` values observed so far (e.g. "asrep_roast_target_list") don't match that taxonomy and
// the full category value space isn't yet characterized. Cheap equality/isnotempty filters (DeviceProduct,
// CrownJewels, Severity != Critical) run before parse_json/mv-expand so rows already at Critical never pay
// the json-parse cost.
let ConfidenceThreshold = 0.8;
PrancerFindings
| where DeviceProduct == 'swarmhack'
| where isnotempty(CrownJewels)
| where Severity != 'Critical'
| extend CrownJewelEntries = parse_json(CrownJewels)
| mv-expand CrownJewelEntry = CrownJewelEntries
| extend
    CrownJewelCategory = tostring(CrownJewelEntry.category),
    CrownJewelConfidence = todouble(CrownJewelEntry.confidence),
    CrownJewelContext = tostring(CrownJewelEntry.context)
| where CrownJewelConfidence >= ConfidenceThreshold
| summarize
    HighConfidenceCategories = make_set(CrownJewelCategory, 20),
    HighConfidenceContexts = make_set(CrownJewelContext, 20),
    MaxCrownJewelConfidence = max(CrownJewelConfidence)
  by FindingId, ConfigId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Title, OriginalSeverity = Severity, RiskScore, Confidence,
     ResourceID, KillChain, CrownJewels, TimeGenerated
| extend
    EscalatedSeverity = 'Critical',
    EscalationReason = strcat(
        'Nominal severity ', OriginalSeverity, ' escalated to Critical: CrownJewels identifies high-confidence (>=',
        tostring(ConfidenceThreshold), ') target(s) - ', tostring(HighConfidenceCategories), ': ',
        tostring(HighConfidenceContexts))

properties.description:
Decomposes KillChain''s free-text stage-arrow format ("Stage A via/to detail -> Stage B via/to detail -> ...")
into a per-finding, per-stage MITRE tactic/technique chain - replacing a static, rule-level, identical-
for-every-finding tactic tag with genuine per-finding mapping. Flags kill chains that are either deep
(4+ stages) or contain a dangerous technique marker (Mimikatz, DCSync, Golden/Silver Ticket, Kerberoast,
ADCS ESC1/2/8, NTDS.dit, Pass-the-Hash). VALIDATION NOTE (2026-08-11): live-tested against real production
data - the query executes cleanly and correctly returns zero matches today, because observed KillChain
values are a flat scan-level execution-mode string ("full"), not a per-finding stage-arrow path. Safe to
ship (no errors, no false positives), but functionally dormant until SwarmHack populates a real per-finding
narrative in KillChain - revisit once that data is confirmed available.
properties.displayName: Kill chain decomposition - deep or dangerous-technique chains
properties.query:
// split() on '->' is cheap; the StageCount/dangerous-marker where-clause runs immediately after split
// and before mv-expand, so only kill chains that already qualify pay the per-stage extract() cost.
let DangerousTechniqueMarkers = dynamic([
    'Mimikatz', 'DCSync', 'Golden Ticket', 'Silver Ticket', 'Kerberoast',
    'ADCS ESC1', 'ADCS ESC2', 'ADCS ESC8', 'NTDS.dit', 'Pass-the-Hash', 'Pass the Hash'
]);
PrancerFindings
| where DeviceProduct == 'swarmhack'
| where isnotempty(KillChain)
| extend KillChainStages = split(KillChain, '->')
| extend StageCount = array_length(KillChainStages)
| where StageCount >= 4 or KillChain has_any (DangerousTechniqueMarkers)
| mv-expand with_itemindex = StageIndex KillChainStages
| extend Stage = trim(' ', tostring(KillChainStages))
| extend
    StageTactic = trim(' ', extract(@'^(.*?)\s+(?:via|to)\s+.*$', 1, Stage)),
    StageDetail = trim(' ', extract(@'^.*?\s+(?:via|to)\s+(.*)$', 1, Stage))
| extend StageIsDangerous = Stage has_any (DangerousTechniqueMarkers)
| summarize
    StageChain = make_list(pack('index', StageIndex, 'tactic', StageTactic, 'detail', StageDetail, 'dangerous', StageIsDangerous)),
    DangerousStageTactics = make_set_if(StageTactic, StageIsDangerous)
  by FindingId, ConfigId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Title, Severity, RiskScore, Confidence, ResourceID,
     KillChain, StageCount, TimeGenerated
| extend
    IsDeepChain = StageCount >= 4,
    HasDangerousTechnique = array_length(DangerousStageTactics) > 0
| extend DecompositionSummary = strcat(
    StageCount, '-stage kill chain',
    iff(IsDeepChain, ' (deep)', ''),
    iff(HasDangerousTechnique, strcat(' - dangerous technique(s) at stage(s): ', tostring(DangerousStageTactics)), ''))

Flags DeviceProduct == sast findings scoped to a curated dangerous-CWE allowlist (SQL Injection=89,
XSS=79, Hardcoded Credentials=798, Broken/Risky Crypto=327, Path Traversal=22, SSRF=918, Insecure
Deserialization=502) that also carry non-empty AlertEvidence, instead of alerting on every SAST finding

properties.query:
// DeviceProduct (not ScanType) is the correct SAST filter - ScanType would be the raw tool name
// (e.g. semgrep). Cheap filters (DeviceProduct, isnotempty(CweId/AlertEvidence)) run before the
// regex-based CweId normalization, since CweId storage format (bare digits vs 'CWE-89') isn't

    CweIdNormalized == '327', 'Broken/Risky Cryptography',
    CweIdNormalized == '22', 'Path Traversal',
    CweIdNormalized == '918', 'Server-Side Request Forgery',
    CweIdNormalized == '502', 'Insecure Deserialization',
    'Other')

properties.description:
Two SCA (DeviceProduct == sca) cases combined into one rule: (1) unpatched-critical-no-fix - CVSSScore
>= 9 with no Solution and no RemediationDescription, i.e. no compensating control is documented, not
just "update the package"; (2) org-wide blast radius - the same vulnerable Title/CweId recurring across
5+ distinct ConfigIds, i.e. a shared dependency or base-image problem invisible at single-finding
severity thresholds.
properties.displayName: SCA critical-unpatched and org-wide blast-radius findings
properties.query:
// DeviceProduct (not ScanType) filters SCA. Both branches filter DeviceProduct=='sca' first; the
// blast-radius branch further filters isnotempty(Title)/isnotempty(CweId) before the dcount/make_set
// aggregation that drives its cost.
let LookbackWindow = 7d;
let BlastRadiusThreshold = 5;
let ScaFindings = PrancerFindings
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
    | where DeviceProduct == 'sca';
let UnpatchedCritical = ScaFindings
    | where CVSSScore >= 9
    | where isempty(Solution) and isempty(RemediationDescription)
    | extend AlertReason = 'unpatched_critical_no_fix', BlastRadiusConfigCount = 1
    | project FindingId, ConfigId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Title, Severity, CweId, CVSSScore, CVSSVector,
               Solution, RemediationDescription, AlertReason, BlastRadiusConfigCount, TimeGenerated;
let BlastRadius = ScaFindings
    | where isnotempty(Title) and isnotempty(CweId)
    | summarize
        BlastRadiusConfigCount = dcount(ConfigId),
        AffectedConfigIds = make_set(ConfigId, 100),
        arg_max(TimeGenerated, FindingId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Severity, CVSSScore, CVSSVector, Solution, RemediationDescription, ConfigId)
      by Title, CweId
    | where BlastRadiusConfigCount >= BlastRadiusThreshold
    | extend AlertReason = 'org_wide_blast_radius'
    | project FindingId, ConfigId, CustomerId, CompanyName, Title, Severity, CweId, CVSSScore, CVSSVector,
               Solution, RemediationDescription, AlertReason, BlastRadiusConfigCount, AffectedConfigIds, TimeGenerated;
UnpatchedCritical
| union BlastRadius
| extend AlertSummary = iff(AlertReason == 'unpatched_critical_no_fix',
    strcat('Critical CVSS ', CVSSScore, ' with no documented fix or remediation'),
    strcat('Same vulnerable component recurring across ', BlastRadiusConfigCount, ' distinct ConfigIds'))

Reframes the finding store from a discovery tool into an accountability tool: flags Critical/High
(SeverityRank <= 2) findings that recur across 3 or more distinct ScanIds for the same ConfigId/Title/
CweId over a 30-day window, i.e. survived multiple scan cycles unremediated. Uses first/last-seen
aggregation to surface how long each finding has been outstanding.
properties.displayName: Critical/High findings persisting across scan cycles unremediated
properties.query:
// This is a process/accountability signal rather than a specific attacker technique, so it runs on a
// daily cadence over a 30-day window rather than near-real-time. SeverityRank <= 2 filters to
// Critical/High before the group-by aggregation that computes scan-cycle persistence.
let LookbackWindow = 30d;
let MinScanCyclesToFlag = 3;
PrancerFindings
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackWindow)
| where SeverityRank <= 2
| where isnotempty(ConfigId) and isnotempty(Title)
| summarize
    ScanCycleCount = dcount(ScanId),
    DistinctScanIds = make_set(ScanId, 50),
    FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
    LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
    arg_max(TimeGenerated, FindingId, Severity, SeverityRank, CompanyName, CustomerId, DeviceProduct, ScanType, ResourceID, ResourceUrl, Solution, RemediationDescription)
  by ConfigId, Title, CweId
| where ScanCycleCount >= MinScanCyclesToFlag
| extend PersistenceDurationDays = datetime_diff('day', LastSeen, FirstSeen)
| extend PersistenceSummary = strcat(
    'Unremediated across ', ScanCycleCount, ' scan cycles over ', PersistenceDurationDays, ' days (', SeverityRank, ')')

properties.description:
Meta-alert monitoring the rate of IsDataQualityIssue-flagged findings per ScanType for spikes against
a trailing 7-day baseline, surfaced alongside ScannerVersion so a scanner-release regression can be
correlated directly rather than requiring someone to notice a slow-moving workbook trend. This is an
operational-telemetry rule, not an attacker-technique detection - tactics/techniques are intentionally
left unmapped.
properties.query:
// Both windows are pre-aggregated with summarize (no parse_json/mv-expand needed - IsDataQualityIssue
// and ScannerVersion are already plain parser-derived columns), then joined on ScanType (a small,
// low-cardinality key) before the volume/rate-delta thresholds are applied.
let CurrentWindow = 1d;
let BaselineWindow = 7d;
let MinVolumeToEvaluate = 20;
let CurrentStats = PrancerFindings
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(CurrentWindow)
    | summarize
        TotalFindings = count(),
        DataQualityIssues = countif(IsDataQualityIssue),
        AffectedScannerVersions = make_set_if(ScannerVersion, IsDataQualityIssue, 20)
      by ScanType
    | extend CurrentIssueRatePct = round(100.0 * DataQualityIssues / TotalFindings, 2);
let BaselineStats = PrancerFindings
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(BaselineWindow + CurrentWindow) .. ago(CurrentWindow))
    | summarize
        BaselineTotalFindings = count(),
        BaselineDataQualityIssues = countif(IsDataQualityIssue)
      by ScanType
    | extend BaselineIssueRatePct = round(100.0 * BaselineDataQualityIssues / BaselineTotalFindings, 2);
CurrentStats
| join kind=inner (BaselineStats) on ScanType
| where TotalFindings >= MinVolumeToEvaluate
| extend RateDeltaPct = CurrentIssueRatePct - BaselineIssueRatePct
| where (BaselineIssueRatePct > 0 and CurrentIssueRatePct >= 2 * BaselineIssueRatePct and RateDeltaPct >= 5.0)
     or (BaselineIssueRatePct == 0 and CurrentIssueRatePct >= 10.0)
| extend SpikeSummary = strcat(
    ScanType, ' data-quality issue rate ', CurrentIssueRatePct, '% (baseline ', BaselineIssueRatePct,
    '%) across scanner version(s) ', tostring(AffectedScannerVersions))
